source_text: Quot adhuc modis probauimus, nihil ex his quae spectaculis deputantur placitum deo esse! at congruens seruo dei quod deo placitum non sit? si omnia propter diabolum institu ta et ex diaboli rebus instructa monstrauimus (nihil enim non diaboli est quicquid dei non est uel deo displicet), hoc erit pompa diaboli, aduersus quem in signaculo fidei eieramus. quod autem eieramus, neque facto neque dicto neque uisu neque conspectu participare debemus. ceterum sic nos eieramus et rescindimus signaculum rescindendo testationem eius. numquid ergo superest, ut ab ipsis ethnicis responsum flagitemus? illi nobis iam renuntient, an liceat Christianis spectaculo uti. atquin hinc uel maxime intelligunt factum Christianum, de repudio spectaculorum. itaque negat manifeste qu per quod agnoscitur tollit. quid autem spei superest in eiusmodi homine? nemo in castra hostium transit nisi proiectis armis suis, nisi destitutis signis et sacramentis principis sui, nisi pactus simul perire.
thought_title: The logic of renunciation: what displeases God is the devil's pomp
orientation: Tertullian has just finished cataloguing the idolatrous and cruel arts of the shows and now draws the conclusion that Christians, having renounced the devil's pomp at baptism, must not participate in it in any way.
pass_a_gloss: By how many ways yet have we proved that nothing of those things which are assigned to the shows is pleasing to God! But is it fitting for a servant of God that which is not pleasing to God? If we have shown all things to have been instituted because of the devil and furnished from the devil's things (for nothing is not of the devil whatever is not of God or displeases God), this will be the devil's pomp, against whom we have sworn in the seal of faith. But what we have sworn, we ought to participate in neither by deed nor by word nor by sight nor by looking at it. Otherwise we thus swear and we rescind the seal by rescinding its testimony. Does anything therefore remain, that we should demand an answer from the pagans themselves? Let them now announce to us whether it is permitted for Christians to use the show. But indeed from this especially they understand a Christian to have been made, from the repudiation of the shows. And so he denies manifestly who destroys that through which he is recognized. But what of hope remains in a man of this sort? No one crosses into the camp of enemies except having thrown away his own weapons, except having abandoned the standards and oaths of his own prince, except having agreed to perish at the same time.

choices.why: Fixed glossary term for the pageantry renounced at baptism; kept literal to preserve the baptismal formula's force.
Fixed glossary term for baptism; literal rendering preserves the metaphor of a seal that can be rescinded.
The verb uti means to make use of or enjoy; 'use' keeps the legal flavor of the question about what is permitted.

choices.english: a Christian to have been made
choices.why: The perfect passive participle factum means 'made' or 'become'; the literal rendering preserves the sense that pagans recognize a Christian by the change that has occurred.
rejected: that someone has become a Christian

choices.why: Sacramentum here means the military oath of allegiance; 'oaths' preserves the military metaphor of the soldier renouncing his commander.

choices.english: having agreed to perish at the same time
choices.why: The perfect participle pactus means having made a pact or agreement; the literal rendering keeps the sense of a deliberate bargain with death.
rejected: having made a pact to perish together
having bargained to perish at once

pass_b_english: How many ways have we now proved that nothing assigned to the shows is pleasing to God! But is what is not pleasing to God fitting for God's servant? If we have shown that all these things were instituted for the devil's sake and furnished from the devil's resources—for whatever is not God's or displeases God is nothing but the devil's—then this is the devil's pomp, against which we swore in the seal of faith. And what we have sworn against, we must not participate in by deed, word, sight, or gaze. Otherwise we swear against it and then rescind the seal by rescinding its testimony.

Does anything remain, then, but to demand an answer from the pagans themselves? Let them announce to us whether Christians are permitted to use the show. Yet it is precisely from the repudiation of shows that they recognize a Christian to have been made. So the one who destroys the mark by which he is recognized plainly denies it. What hope remains for such a person? No one crosses into the enemy's camp except by throwing away his own weapons, abandoning the standards and oaths of his own prince, and agreeing to perish at the same time.

last_rejected.quote: Let them announce to us whether Christians are permitted to use the show
last_rejected.source_quote: illi nobis iam renuntient, an liceat Christianis spectaculo uti
last_rejected.why: 'renuntient' means 'renounce/declare' here; pagans should answer whether Christians may use shows, not announce permission.
last_rejected.fix: Let them now declare to us whether Christians are permitted to use the show.

last_rejected.quote: So the one who destroys the mark by which he is recognized plainly denies it.
last_rejected.source_quote: itaque negat manifeste qu per quod agnoscitur tollit.
last_rejected.why: 'qu' should read 'qui'; meaning is 'he plainly denies the very thing by which he is recognized, by destroying it.'
last_rejected.fix: So he plainly denies the very thing by which he is recognized, by destroying it.
last_rejected.ruling: qu ≈ qui; English captures ‘denies by destroying the mark by which he is recognized’.

last_rejected.quote: abandoning the standards and oaths of his own prince
last_rejected.source_quote: nisi destitutis signis et sacramentis principis sui
last_rejected.why: Latin 'sacramentis' means sacraments, not oaths; the translation changes the meaning.
last_rejected.fix: abandoning the signs and sacraments of his own prince
last_rejected.ruling: Latin 'sacramentum' in Tertullian's military context means 'military oath'; 'oaths' is correct, not the later theological sense.

polish.changed: Clarified the speaker's progression from proof to application, kept the baptismal renunciation phrase consistent as 'the devil's pomp,' and broke the argument into two paragraphs where the thought turns from the Christian's obligation to the pagan witness.

notes.why: Inconsistent rendering of same Latin phrase; reader may miss they are identical.

notes.quote: renounced the devil and his pomp and his angels

variants.text: the devil and his pomp and his angels

notes.why: The baptismal renunciation formula shifts wording across sections, confusing a reader about the fixed liturgical phrase.
notes.fix: Use one consistent phrase for the baptismal renunciation throughout.
